dedupe_keys.name: h21 leeds city gate converting the leeds natural gas network to 100 hydrogen northern gas networks feasibility study 2016

description: This case study is the executive summary of the H21 Leeds City Gate project, a July 2016 feasibility study led by Northern Gas Networks on converting the natural gas distribution network of Leeds, one of the largest UK cities, to 100% hydrogen. The study looked at the technical and economic case, aiming to minimise disruption to customers and to deliver heat at the same cost as natural gas. It modelled the medium and low pressure networks with the network analysis software and data used by the operator and found sufficient capacity for hydrogen with relatively minor upgrades. Demand was put at 678 MW on average and 3,180 MW at the 1 in 20 peak hour, with supply from four steam methane reformers with 90% carbon capture at Teesside, salt cavern storage and a hydrogen transmission system, and a three-year incremental conversion through the summer months. Access: the executive summary is a free PDF on the Northern Gas Networks site and the full report is listed at the Hydrogen Knowledge Centre; no licence is stated. Coverage is one UK city. Caveats: only the executive summary was read, and the numbers are project assumptions from 2016. It suits design and investment appraisal studies of gas network conversion, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: H21 Leeds City Gate: converting the Leeds natural gas network to 100% hydrogen (Northern Gas Networks feasibility study, 2016)
outcomes: The study concluded that the Leeds gas distribution network has enough capacity for 100% hydrogen with relatively minor upgrades, can be converted incrementally over a three-year summer programme with minimal disruption, and that Leeds' demand (average 678 MW, peak hour 3,180 MW, 5.9 TWh a year) could be met by four steam methane reformers with 90% carbon capture at Teesside plus salt cavern storage at Teesside and the East Humber coast, delivering heat at the cost of natural gas.
